experiment: For every successful campaign block/wavelength, compare deterministic native-grid KFS to the persisted native MC mean; then compare deterministic 60/120 m coarse-grid KFS at the productive boundary to the grouped native deterministic solution; finally compare aggregated MC mean to aggregated deterministic KFS. This separates the coarse representation/boundary-cell effect from the nonlinear Monte Carlo mean already present in method v4.
interpretation: The nonlinear partial-Monte-Carlo mean differs materially from deterministic KFS even on the productive native grid; this is not a new aggregation artifact.

The aggregation-specific deterministic coarse-representation plus boundary-cell effect is about 4.6% median at 60 m and 5.6% median at 120 m, consistent with the approximately 5-6% median same-boundary MC-vs-MC campaign differences.
The aggregation-specific effect is strongly event/block dependent, with p95 around 21-22% and maxima above 40%, so a median-only preservation argument would be unsafe.

High-boundary native-grid experiments show larger campaign-wide lower-column changes than this aggregation-only structural effect, making boundary-condition validity the dominant next scientific question.
decision: Treat aggregation discretization/boundary-cell representation and high-boundary validity as separate R&D dimensions. Do not tune an aggregation width to compensate for high-boundary bias.
